core_obligations: Apply the vanishing criterion with the set of affine objects and the standard affine coverings, using that those coverings compute Cech cohomology, to get vanishing of higher cohomology of the associated module on affines (proof lines 3012-3028).

On a separated object, use the Cech spectral sequence and the affine results to identify the cohomology on the site with the cohomology of the pullback, which proves the statement when the base is separated (proof lines 3030-3051).

In general, build a comparison map between the derived global sections of the associated module and of the original module by restricting an injective resolution and lifting along an exact complex, and check exactness on affines using the vanishing already obtained (proof lines 3055-3082).

Compare the two Cech spectral sequences over an affine open covering, whose second pages are identified because intersections of affine opens in a separated scheme are affine, and conclude that the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism (proof lines 3083-3105).
proof_roadmap: The comparison map of resolutions (proof lines 3055-3082).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-coherent sheaf on a scheme and a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, the proposition identifies the cohomology computed on the small Zariski site with the cohomology on the big tau-site and on the small etale site (statement lines 2989-3010). The proof applies the vanishing criterion on a basis to conclude that higher cohomology of the associated module vanishes on affine objects, using that standard affine coverings compute Cech cohomology of a quasi-coherent module (proof lines 3012-3028). It then compares Cech and ordinary cohomology on separated objects, which already proves the statement when the base is separated (proof lines 3030-3051). For the general case the author constructs a map between the two derived global section complexes via a comparison of injective resolutions, verifies exactness of the relevant complex on affine opens using the vanishing just obtained, and compares the two Cech spectral sequences whose second pages are identified because intersections of affines in a separated scheme are affine, concluding that the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism (proof lines 3055-3105). The claim is H3: the first half is a clean application of the vanishing criterion, and the second half builds a comparison map of resolutions together with a spectral sequence argument of its own.
